quotes.text: The AI Gateway is the reception desk and the security desk at the front. It checks who is coming in, applies the rules and records where requests go before they reach the rest of the building.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy for the gateway's role as a single control point.

quotes.text: A wrong answer from a model confuses someone, but an agent using the wrong tool can expose data, change a record, or trigger a process it should never touch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concisely explains why agents raise the risk profile compared with chat models.

quotes.text: Each agent should have its own identity. That way you can see which agent called a tool, revoke access for one agent without breaking others and apply different rules.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The problem isn't just that the company spent money. The wrong workload took capacity from the workload that mattered most.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: From one chatbot to dozens of AI tools

takeaways: Microsoft AI Gateway is a set of Azure API Management features that puts one managed control point in front of AI models, MCP tools, agents and business APIs.
Routing behind a stable endpoint lets platform teams change models, regions or providers and add backup paths without changing every application.
Per-agent identities, narrow approved tools, safety checks and token limits and quotas keep agents in bounds and make AI usage and cost traceable.
hook: When every team connects its own AI app straight to a model provider, keys leak, costs blur and nobody can say what an agent actually did. This episode is for platform, security and AI teams scaling beyond a single chatbot. You learn how Microsoft AI Gateway in Azure API Management centralizes routing, identity, safety checks and token limits for models, tools and agents.
